findings.title: Metric actor_email changed by email fallback
findings.problem: decide() reassigns decided_by_email = actor at queue_service.py:726-727 when the acting id has no users row and no email was passed, and the same variable is then passed as actor_email to track_marketplace_metric at :881. The spec non-goal (spec.md:88) says no change to the decision metrics, and the spec decision (spec.md:101) keeps the metric actor on the raw values.
findings.impact: For an actor with no users row and no email (IdP users without an email claim, admin calls with decided_by_id None), the decision metric's actor_email changes from None to the username/id string. The path is live on every such decision after commit; it deviates from the approved spec and changes metric data that downstream dashboards group by.
findings.recommendation: Keep the caller's email for the metric: compute the fallback into a separate variable (e.g. `ledger_email = decided_by_email or (actor if recorded_id is None else None)`), use it for the `MarketplaceReviewDecision.decided_by_email` and the `_record_activity_event` `actor_email`, and pass the original `decided_by_email` to `track_marketplace_metric`. Add an assertion to the DB-free decide() unit test that the metric receives `actor_email=None` when no email was passed.
findings.check_notes: queue_service.py:727 computes ledger_email, used at :804 and :826; :881 passes the raw decided_by_email to the metric; no reassignment of decided_by_email remains. A test asserts the metric gets actor_email None.

fix.change: decide() puts the actor-string fallback in a separate ledger_email for the ledger row and activity event; track_marketplace_metric gets the caller's raw decided_by_email

findings.title: Removed None guard in _snapshot_actor
findings.problem: _snapshot_actor calls _recorded_user_id, which discards the loaded UserDB, then calls session.get(UserDB, actor_id) again and dereferences user.email / user.name with no None check. The SQLAlchemy identity map is weak-referencing, so the comment 'Served from the identity map' does not hold: the second get can re-query and return None. The previous code guarded `if user is not None`.
findings.impact: Trigger is narrow: the user's row must be deleted and committed by another transaction between the two adjacent lookups. Then an AttributeError is raised before the activity insert's savepoint and aborts the whole decision. It also costs an extra users query per decision.
findings.recommendation: Have the rule return the loaded row (or keep the `if user is not None` guard), so _snapshot_actor reads email/name from the object it already has and drops actor_id when it is gone; correct the identity-map comment.
findings.check_notes: _snapshot_actor (:1275) uses the UserDB from _recorded_user: one lookup, actor_id dropped when None, no second session.get; the identity-map comment is removed.

fix.change: New _recorded_user returns the loaded UserDB row; _snapshot_actor reads email/name from it with one lookup and drops actor_id when it is None; _recorded_user_id delegates to it
